claims.text: THE CONTRACTOR CARVE-OUT, in regulation. 32 CFR 117.6(b) (responsibilities of the Director, DCSA) verbatim: 'The Director, DCSA, will be relieved of this oversight function for DoD special access programs (SAPs) when the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense approves a carve-out provision in accordance with DoDD 5205.07, "DoD SAP Policy".' The preceding sentence establishes what is being relieved: DCSA 'Provides security oversight of the NISP as the DoD CSO on behalf of DoD components and those non-DoD executive branch agencies who enter into agreements with DoD.'

The carve-out is therefore not a classification device but an INSPECTION device: it removes the one federal agency that would otherwise physically visit, inspect, and record a cleared contractor facility performing the classified work. Nothing else in Part 117 substitutes an alternative external inspector; oversight reverts inside the SAP's own chain.

32 CFR 117.3(b) defines ACCM verbatim: 'ACCM are security measures used by USG agencies to safeguard classified intelligence or operations when normal measures are insufficient to achieve strict need-to-know controls and where SAP controls are not required.' ACCM is thus a SAP-like access control that by definition sits outside the SAP reporting statutes.

32 CFR 117.3(b) defines SAP verbatim: 'SAP means any program that is established to control access and distribution and to provide protection for particularly sensitive classified information beyond that normally required for TOP SECRET, SECRET, or CONFIDENTIAL information.'

32 CFR 117.23 is titled 'Supplement to this rule: Security Requirements for Alternative Compensatory Control Measures (ACCM), Special Access Programs (SAPs), Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI), Restricted Data (RD), Formerly Restricted Data (FRD), Transclassified Foreign Nuclear Information (TFNI), and Naval Nuclear Propulsion Information (NNPI).' 117.23(a)(1) verbatim: 'The contractor will comply with the security measures reflected in this section and other documents specifically referenced, when applied by the GCA or designee as part of a contract. Acceptance of the contract security measures is a prerequisite to any negotiations leading to program participation and an area accreditation (e.g., an SCI facility or SAP facility accreditation).'

32 CFR 117.6(b) cites, as the controlling authority for the carve-out, the pre-2024 version of DoDD 5205.07 at the URL https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodd/520507p.pdf?ver=2020-02-04-142942-827 — i.e. the 1 July 2010 directive as amended. The regulation has not been updated to cite the 12 September 2024 reissuance.

claims.text: The rule's source line is '85 FR 83312, Dec. 21, 2020', which dates the codified carve-out provision to the December 2020 NISPOM rulemaking.

32 CFR 117.3(b): 'SAP means any program that is established to control access and distribution and to provide protection for particularly sensitive classified information beyond that normally required for TOP SECRET, SECRET, or CONFIDENTIAL information. A SAP can be created or continued only as authorized by a senior agency official delegated such authority pursuant to E.O. 13526.'
32 CFR 117.3(b) lists SAP information as 'proscribed information' together with TOP SECRET information, COMSEC information, Restricted Data and SCI.

32 CFR 117.23(d)(1): 'DoD SAP contracts. Contractors will implement the security requirements for SAPs codified in SAP-related policy, when established by contract. These documents include, but are not limited to, statutes, E.O.s, CSA directives, instructions, manuals, regulations, standards, memorandums, and other SAP security related policy documents.'

32 CFR 117.23(a)(2) provides that where a CSA-created program requires measures exceeding the rule's standards, 'the CSA-imposed higher standards specifically detailed in the contract or conveyed through other applicable directives will be binding on USG and contractor participants.'

32 CFR 117.3(b) defines ACCM as 'security measures used by USG agencies to safeguard classified intelligence or operations when normal measures are insufficient to achieve strict need-to-know controls and where SAP controls are not required.'

Because 117.23(d)(1) exports the substantive SAP security requirements into contract documents, the actual rules governing a contractor holding SAP material are not published anywhere in the Code of Federal Regulations and are not obtainable without the contract. Reasoning: the regulation defers to unspecified 'SAP security related policy documents' established by contract.

desc: The NISPOM ceased to be a DoD manual and became a federal regulation with the codification of 32 CFR Part 117, which now carries the rules binding every cleared contractor in the United States. For this board its value is threefold. First, it supplies the operative regulatory definition of a SAP: 'SAP means any program that is established to control access and distribution and to provide protection for particularly sensitive classified information beyond that normally required for TOP SECRET, SECRET, or CONFIDENTIAL information. A SAP can be created or continued only as authorized by a senior agency official delegated such authority pursuant to E.O. 13526.' Second, it contains the carve-out at 117.6(b)(3). Third, section 117.23 is the supplement for ACCM, SAPs, SCI, Restricted Data, Formerly Restricted Data, Transclassified Foreign Nuclear Information and Naval Nuclear Propulsion Information, and its paragraph (d)(1) provides that for DoD SAP contracts 'Contractors will implement the security requirements for SAPs codified in SAP-related policy, when established by contract' - a formulation that pushes the actual security rules out of the regulation and into contract documents that are not public. Part 117 also treats SAP information as 'proscribed information' alongside TOP SECRET, COMSEC, Restricted Data and SCI, which triggers the National Interest Determination process for entities under foreign ownership, control or influence. The whole rule is issued under the authority of section 201 of Executive Order 12829.
